text: Recorded at #972's merge, which finished #959's build by hand after the factory's reviewer found two parser defects. A plumbing review's verdict is read by a reader deliberately stricter than Markdown, which holds the build whenever it can't place the verdict, rather than an imitation of Markdown: exactly one line whose first word is VERDICT, in any case, and it must be the last non-blank line, exactly VERDICT: approve or VERDICT: changes needed. Fences after a quote or list marker, or indented by a tab or four spaces, hold outright; a fence indented one to three spaces must keep its indentation and close at exactly it, and a fence open at the verdict holds. HTML outside a fence holds. Unless a blank line or a closed fence comes right before the verdict, the build holds if any line of the paragraph before it starts with indentation, a quote, a list marker or a footnote, or holds a table's bar. The reviewer is asked for a blank line before its verdict. Checked against a CommonMark parser with GitHub's tables and footnotes over 37 million random replies with no acceptance outside a top-level paragraph, and every one of 128 real factory reviews still decides as written.
